title: Internal and external issues
goal: The organization identifies and keeps current the internal and external issues, including climate change where relevant, that affect its ability to achieve its security outcomes.
note: Clause only. Climate wording from the 2024 amendment sits in this control.

title: Interested parties and their requirements
goal: The organization identifies the parties that have a stake in its security, determines their requirements, including any climate-related ones, and decides which of those it will address.
note: Clause only. Split from issues (GOV-01) because the test differs: issues register versus interested-party register.

title: Scope of the security program
goal: The organization defines and documents the boundaries and applicability of its security management program, taking account of issues, stakeholder requirements and dependencies.
note: Clause only.

title: Security management system operated
goal: The organization establishes, runs and maintains a security management system, with the processes it needs and the way they interact.
note: Clause only.

title: Leadership commitment
goal: Top management shows leadership of the security program by aligning it to strategy, building it into business processes, making sure it achieves its intended outcomes, directing and supporting the people who run it and supporting other managers in their own leadership.
note: Clause only.

title: Security policy set
goal: The organization maintains a management-approved set of security policies, headed by a top-level policy that reflects the organization's context, that is published, acknowledged by personnel and relevant outside parties, and reviewed at planned intervals.
note: Merge: clause security policy (top-level policy) and Annex control on policies for information security. Same goal, owner and test.

title: Security roles and responsibilities
goal: The organization defines and allocates security roles, responsibilities and authorities to named people, including responsibility for program conformity and reporting to top management.
note: Merge: clause on roles and authorities and Annex control on security roles. Same goal, owner and test.

title: Team members aligned with security policy
goal: The organization requires every team member to work in line with its security policies and procedures, and shows the requirement has reached each team.

title: Specialist security forums
goal: The organization keeps contact with specialist security forums and professional groups and uses what it learns.

title: Risks and opportunities of the program
goal: The organization determines the risks and opportunities that bear on the security program, plans actions for them, builds those actions into its processes and checks they work.
note: Clause only. General planning step. Risk assessment and treatment detail sits in the risk domain.

title: Security objectives
goal: The organization sets measurable security objectives at relevant functions, consistent with policy, and plans what will be done, with what resources, by whom, by when and how results are evaluated.
note: Clause only.

title: Planned changes to the program
goal: The organization carries out any needed change to its security management system in a planned way.
note: Clause only. Covers planning of changes.

title: Resources for the program
goal: The organization determines and provides the resources needed to establish, run, maintain and improve its security program.
note: Clause only.

title: Security communication plan
goal: The organization decides what security matters it communicates, when, to whom and how, inside and outside the organization, and follows that plan.
note: Clause only. Narrowed in round 2: incident and recovery communication moved to UC-INC-43.

title: Documented information control
goal: The organization keeps the documented information its security program needs, and controls how it is created, approved, updated, distributed, protected, retained and disposed of.
note: Clause only.

title: Security processes planned and run
goal: The organization plans, runs and controls the processes needed to meet its security requirements against set criteria, and keeps records showing they ran as planned.
note: Clause only. Narrowed in round 2: change control re-mapped to UC-SDC-09, externally provided processes to UC-SUP-05.

title: Performance monitoring and measurement
goal: The organization decides what security performance to measure and how (valid, comparable methods), when and by whom it is measured and analyzed, evaluates the results and keeps evidence.
note: Clause only.

title: Management review
goal: Top management reviews the security program at planned intervals using defined inputs and records decisions on improvement and needed changes.
note: Clause only.

title: Continual improvement
goal: The organization continually improves the suitability, adequacy and effectiveness of its security program.
note: Clause only. Kept apart from corrective action (GOV-20) because the test differs.

title: Nonconformity and corrective action
goal: The organization reacts to nonconformities, corrects them, removes their causes, checks the fix worked and keeps records.
note: Clause only.

title: Risk assessment method
goal: The organization defines a repeatable risk assessment method with set acceptance criteria and criteria for performing assessments that identifies risks and their owners and ranks them by likelihood and impact.
note: Clause only. Method, not the performing of assessments (RSK-04).

title: Risk treatment plan
goal: The organization chooses a treatment for each assessed risk, determines the controls needed, and gets the treatment plan approved and residual risk accepted in writing by those accountable for each risk.
note: Clause only. Split from the applicability statement (RSK-03) because the test differs.

title: Statement of applicable controls
goal: The organization keeps a documented statement of which controls apply, why each is included or left out and whether each is implemented, checked against a reference control set so none is missed.
note: Clause only. Split from treatment plan (RSK-02).

title: Risk assessments performed
goal: The organization performs risk assessments at planned intervals and when significant change occurs, and keeps the results.
note: Clause only.

title: Risk treatment carried out
goal: The organization carries out its risk treatment plan and keeps the results.
note: Clause only.

title: Legal and contractual requirements register
goal: The organization identifies and documents the legal, regulatory and contractual requirements that bear on its information security, records how each is met, and keeps the list current.

title: Intellectual property and licensing
goal: The organization protects intellectual property rights, including using software only from legitimate sources and staying within license terms.

title: Record of personal data processing
goal: The organization keeps a current record of its processing of personal data for the scope of its program.
note: Split in round 2: responsibility for privacy moved to UC-RSK-11; identifying applicable privacy laws re-mapped to UC-RSK-06.

title: Independent review of the security program
goal: The organization has its approach to security independently reviewed through a planned internal audit program and other independent reviews, and reports the results to management.
note: Merge: clause on internal audit and Annex control on independent review. Same goal, owner and test.

title: Practice checked against policy
goal: The organization checks, on a set cycle, that the day-to-day work of each team where security controls apply follows its documented security policies and standards, and acts on any gap.

title: Responsibility for privacy assigned
goal: The organization assigns and records responsibility for privacy and the protection of personal data.
note: Split from UC-RSK-08 in round 2 so it has its own test.

title: Asset inventory
goal: The organization keeps a current inventory of information and associated assets, including software, services and systems, each with an assigned owner.

title: Acceptable use rules acknowledged
goal: The organization sets rules for acceptable and prohibited use of its information and assets, tells users their use is monitored, and has users acknowledge the rules.
note: Split in round 2: handling rules by classification level moved to UC-AST-13.

title: Return of assets
goal: Personnel and external parties return all organizational assets when they leave or change role, contract or agreement.

title: Information classification
goal: The organization classifies information by its confidentiality, integrity, availability and stakeholder needs, using a defined scheme.

title: Information labeling
goal: The organization labels information in line with its classification scheme.

title: Information transfer
goal: The organization sets rules, agreements and technical settings for every channel used to transfer information, matched to its sensitivity.

title: Records retention schedule
goal: The organization defines the types of records it keeps, how long each is kept and how each must be stored, based on legal and contractual needs.
note: Split in round 2: protection of records moved to UC-AST-14.

title: Information deletion
goal: The organization deletes information from systems, devices and media when it is no longer needed, by a defined method, and keeps proof.

title: Data masking
goal: The organization masks, pseudonymizes or anonymizes data where its rules and applicable law require.

title: Data leakage prevention
goal: The organization finds the sensitive information that could leak and the channels it could leak through, applies preventive measures to them and acts on alerts.

title: Storage media management
goal: The organization manages storage media through acquisition, use, transport and disposal in line with classification and handling rules.
note: Disposal records for media are also mapped to AST-12.

title: Sanitization before disposal or reuse
goal: The organization verifies that equipment and media holding data have been wiped or destroyed before disposal or reuse, and keeps proof.
note: Equipment disposal control. Also reached by the disposal atom of the storage media record.

title: Handling rules by classification level
goal: The organization documents how information at each classification level is stored, shared, transported and disposed of.
note: Split from UC-AST-02 in round 2 so it has its own test.

title: Protection of records
goal: The organization protects stored records from loss, tampering and unauthorized access for their retention period.
note: Split from UC-AST-07 in round 2 so it has its own test.

title: Access control rules
goal: The organization sets and applies rules for physical and logical access to information and assets based on business and security needs.

title: Identity life cycle
goal: The organization manages the full life cycle of identities, links each to one person or an owned non-person account and removes identities of people who have left.

title: Credential issue, reset and revocation
goal: The organization controls how authentication credentials are issued, reset and revoked, and guides users on keeping them secret.
note: Split in round 2: default credentials moved to UC-IAM-13.

title: Access provisioning
goal: The organization grants or changes access only after documented approval and in line with the access rules.
note: Split from access rights record: provisioning and change. Review (IAM-05) and removal (IAM-06) have different tests.

title: Periodic access review
goal: The organization reviews access rights at a set frequency and removes access that is no longer appropriate.
note: Split from access rights record.

title: Access removal on leaving or role change
goal: The organization removes or adjusts access promptly when people leave or change role, within the timeframe it has set.
note: Split from access rights record.

title: Segregation of duties
goal: The organization separates conflicting duties, or applies compensating measures where separation is not possible.

title: Privileged access
goal: The organization authorizes, limits, records and regularly reviews privileged access rights, held in accounts separate from everyday use.

title: Information access restriction
goal: The organization restricts access to information and functions in each system to what each role is authorized to use.
note: Kept apart from the access rules (IAM-01) because the test is system configuration, not policy.

title: Access to source code and build tools
goal: The organization limits read and write access to source code, development tools and libraries to those authorized and requires review before changes merge.

title: Secure authentication
goal: The organization enforces authentication strength by system sensitivity, including multi-factor where needed, and protects log-on against guessing.

title: Privileged utility programs
goal: The organization restricts utility programs that can override system or application controls to authorized people and logs their use.

title: Default credentials changed on installation
goal: The organization changes default vendor credentials when systems and devices are installed.
note: Split from UC-IAM-03 in round 2 so it has its own test.

title: Use of encryption
goal: The organization defines where encryption is required and which methods are approved, and applies it to data at rest and in transit accordingly.
note: Split from cryptography record: encryption use. Key management (CRY-02) has a different test.

title: Cryptographic key management
goal: The organization manages cryptographic keys across their life, from generation to destruction, holds them in a controlled store and rotates them as set.
note: Split from cryptography record.

title: Endpoint device protection
goal: The organization sets security requirements for user endpoint devices and verifies that devices meet them.

title: Secure configuration baselines
goal: The organization defines secure configuration baselines for hardware, software, services and networks, monitors drift from them and reviews the baselines.

title: Network security management
goal: The organization secures and manages networks and network devices, keeps an accurate network diagram and reviews firewall rules.

title: Security of network services
goal: The organization documents and monitors the security features, service levels and requirements of the network services it uses.

title: Network segregation
goal: The organization separates groups of services, users and systems into network segments by trust level and enforces the allowed traffic between them.

title: Web filtering
goal: The organization controls access to external websites to reduce exposure to malicious content, including for remote users.

title: Clock synchronization
goal: The organization synchronizes system clocks to approved time sources.

title: Software installation control
goal: The organization controls who may install software on operational systems, from which sources and with what approval, and enforces it technically.

title: Secure remote working
goal: The organization sets security requirements for remote working and enforces them technically for remote access.

title: Event logging
goal: The organization produces, collects centrally and retains logs of defined security-relevant events for each system type.
note: Split from logging record: generation and retention. Protection (OPS-02) has a different test.

title: Log protection
goal: The organization protects logs from tampering and unauthorized access, including from administrators of the logged systems.
note: Split from logging record.

title: Monitoring for anomalous activity
goal: The organization monitors networks, systems and applications for anomalous behavior, including unauthorized devices and wireless access points, and raises alerts for analysis.
note: Also carries the log analysis atom of the logging record. Alert analysis, correlation and routing sit in UC-OPS-41.

title: Vulnerability management
goal: The organization gathers vulnerability information, scans systems, assesses exposure and fixes findings within set deadlines or formally accepts the risk.
note: Split from vulnerability record: scanning and fixing. Penetration testing (OPS-05) has a different test.

title: Penetration testing
goal: The organization has internet-facing systems penetration tested at least yearly and tracks findings to closure.
note: Split from vulnerability record.

title: Authorization of assurance testing on live systems
goal: The organization plans audit and assurance tests on operational systems and has responsible management approve them in advance.

title: Malware protection
goal: The organization defines, deploys and keeps current protection against malware on in-scope systems.
note: Malware awareness atom is carried by PPL-03.

title: Threat intelligence
goal: The organization collects and analyzes threat information, produces threat intelligence and acts on it.

title: Documented operating procedures
goal: The organization documents operating procedures for key IT activities and keeps current versions available to those who need them.

title: Capacity management
goal: The organization defines capacity requirements for critical systems, monitors resource use and adjusts capacity before limits are reached.

title: Security in projects
goal: The organization requires security requirements and risks to be addressed at defined stages of every project.

title: Secure development process
goal: The organization sets security rules for each phase of development and shows they are followed on releases.

title: Application security requirements
goal: The organization identifies, specifies and approves security requirements for applications it builds or buys.

title: Secure engineering principles
goal: The organization documents and keeps current principles for engineering secure systems and applies them in design.

title: Secure coding
goal: The organization applies a secure coding standard to its software and checks code changes by review or automated scanning before release.
note: Developer training atom is carried by PPL-04.

title: Security testing and acceptance
goal: The organization defines security tests for each stage of development and requires results and acceptance sign-off before release.

title: Outsourced development oversight
goal: The organization sets security requirements for outsourced development and monitors and reviews the work.

title: Environment separation
goal: The organization separates development, test and production environments, limits developer access to production and secures non-production to the level of the data it holds.

title: Change management
goal: The organization subjects changes to systems and facilities to recorded assessment, authorization, testing and rollback planning, including emergency changes.

title: Test data protection
goal: The organization selects, authorizes, protects and removes test data so production or personal data is not used in testing without approval.

title: Physical security perimeters
goal: The organization defines and uses physical perimeters to protect areas holding information and assets.

title: Physical entry and visitor control
goal: The organization controls entry to secure areas and records and escorts visitors.
note: Split in round 2: access rights review and leaver badge removal moved to UC-PHY-13.

title: Securing offices, rooms and facilities
goal: The organization specifies and puts in place physical security for offices, rooms and facilities.

title: Physical security monitoring
goal: The organization monitors premises for unauthorized physical access and responds to alerts.

title: Physical and environmental threat protection
goal: The organization assesses physical and environmental threats for each site and installs and maintains protection against them.

title: Working in secure areas
goal: The organization sets rules for working in secure areas and makes authorized people aware of them.

title: Clear desk and clear screen
goal: The organization sets and enforces rules that keep papers, removable media and unattended screens from exposing information.

title: Equipment siting and protection
goal: The organization sites and protects equipment to reduce environmental risk and unauthorized access.

title: Assets off premises
goal: The organization sets rules for protecting assets taken off premises and protects portable devices with encryption and remote wipe.

title: Supporting utilities
goal: The organization protects processing facilities from power and other utility failures and maintains the protection.

title: Cabling security
goal: The organization protects power, data and communications cabling from interception, interference and damage.

title: Scheduled equipment maintenance
goal: The organization maintains in-scope equipment on a schedule and only through authorized personnel.
note: Split in round 2: clearing data before repair moved to UC-PHY-14.

title: Physical access rights review and leaver removal
goal: The organization reviews physical access rights on a defined cycle and removes access for people who leave.
note: Split from UC-PHY-02 in round 2 so it has its own test.

title: Data cleared before equipment leaves for repair
goal: The organization clears or protects sensitive information on equipment before it is sent off site for maintenance or repair.
note: Split from UC-PHY-12 in round 2 so it has its own test.

title: Pre-employment screening
goal: The organization carries out background checks, scaled to role risk, on candidates before they join and re-checks when its rules require.

title: Terms of employment
goal: The organization states security responsibilities of the individual and the organization in employment and contractor agreements, and has them signed.

title: Security awareness
goal: The organization delivers security awareness to all personnel and relevant outside parties, covering policy, individual contribution, consequences of non-compliance and common threats such as phishing and malware, and refreshes it when policies change.
note: Merge: clause on awareness and the all-staff element of the Annex awareness and training control. Role-based training split to PPL-04 because the test differs.

title: Role-based security training
goal: The organization gives people in technical, privileged and other high-risk roles training matched to their duties, such as secure coding for developers.
note: Split from Annex awareness and training record.

title: Competence of security personnel
goal: The organization determines the competence needed by people who affect security performance, ensures they have it, takes action where they do not and keeps evidence.
note: Clause only.

title: Disciplinary process
goal: The organization has a formal, communicated disciplinary process for security policy violations.

title: Responsibilities after leaving
goal: The organization defines and communicates the security responsibilities that continue after employment ends or changes.

title: Confidentiality agreements
goal: The organization has staff and relevant external parties sign confidentiality agreements that reflect its protection needs, and reviews the templates.

title: Supplier inventory and risk tiering
goal: The organization identifies its suppliers, rates their security risk and keeps a register of those with access to its information or systems.
note: Split from supplier relationships record: register and risk tiering. Due diligence (SUP-02) has a different test.

title: Supplier due diligence
goal: The organization completes a security assessment of a supplier before contract signature or access is granted.
note: Split from supplier relationships record.

title: Supplier security agreements
goal: The organization agrees security requirements with each supplier in the contract, including the scope of access and data granted, scaled to supplier type and risk.

title: ICT supply chain risk
goal: The organization requires ICT suppliers to pass security requirements to their own suppliers and disclose critical components, and assesses the chain of key suppliers.

title: Supplier service review
goal: The organization reviews each supplier's services at an interval set by risk tier and whenever the scope of service changes.
note: Kept as one control in round 2: one review requirement with two triggers, a set interval and a change to the scope of service.

title: Cloud service security governance
goal: The organization governs the selection, use and management of cloud services, including shared responsibilities and provider assurance.
note: Split in round 2: cloud exit plans moved to UC-SUP-07.

title: Cloud exit plans
goal: The organization keeps an exit plan for each critical cloud service, covering return and deletion of its data.
note: Split from UC-SUP-06 in round 2 so it has its own test.

title: Incident management plan and roles
goal: The organization documents an incident management plan covering detection through closure, with incident roles assigned to people who have contact details.
note: Split in round 2: communicating and exercising the plan moved to UC-INC-09.

title: Event triage and classification
goal: The organization assesses security events against written criteria and decides whether each is an incident, with severity.

title: Incident response and closure
goal: The organization responds to incidents under documented procedures covering containment, eradication, recovery and escalation, records the work and closes each incident.
note: Split from incident response record: response. Notification duties (INC-04) have a different test.

title: Incident notification duties
goal: The organization decides who may notify authorities and other parties of incidents, within what timelines, and notifies in time where a legal or contractual duty applies.
note: Split from incident response record. Also carries the authorization atom of the authorities contact record.

title: Learning from incidents
goal: The organization reviews significant incidents and tracks the resulting control improvements to completion.

title: Evidence preservation
goal: The organization identifies, collects and preserves evidence of security events with chain of custody.

title: Contact with authorities
goal: The organization keeps a current list of relevant authorities and verifies it regularly.

title: Reporting of security events by personnel
goal: The organization gives personnel a published channel to report observed or suspected security events promptly and tells them what to report.

title: Incident plan communicated and exercised
goal: The organization communicates its incident plan and roles to those who carry them out and exercises the plan.
note: Split from UC-INC-01 in round 2 so it has its own test.

title: Security during disruption
goal: The organization plans how security controls are maintained, or compensated, during a disruption.

title: Recovery objectives and plans
goal: The organization sets recovery time and recovery point objectives for critical IT services from an impact analysis and keeps recovery plans for them.
note: Split from ICT readiness record: objectives and plans. Testing (RES-03) has a different test.

title: Recovery plan testing
goal: The organization tests its IT recovery plans at least yearly, compares results with the recovery objectives and acts on gaps.
note: Split from ICT readiness record.

title: Backup operation
goal: The organization sets a backup policy covering scope, frequency, retention, storage and protection, runs backups to it and investigates failures.
note: Split from backup record: operation. Restore testing (RES-05) has a different test.

title: Restore testing
goal: The organization tests restoring backups at the frequency its policy sets and records the results.
note: Split from backup record.

title: Redundancy for critical systems
goal: The organization defines availability requirements for critical systems and documents the redundancy that meets them, leaving no single point of failure.
note: Split in round 2: failover testing moved to UC-RES-07.

title: Failover testing
goal: The organization tests failover of critical systems, or observes it in a real event, and compares the results with the availability requirements.
note: Split from UC-RES-06 in round 2 so it has its own test.
